newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals seen opening lower.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals seen opening lower.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious were called to open weaker Tuesday as gold drifted lower overnight in quiet trading with bullion fixed below $320 an ounce in London.
COMEX August gold was called to open off $0.50 to $1.50 an ounce from Monday's close at $320.80, after trading between $320.70 and $319.60 in overnight ACCESS trade.
In London gold was fixed at $319.00 an ounce on Tuesday morning, compared with $321.70 on Monday afternoon.
Bullion was quoted at $318.70/$319.00 by dealers.
COMEX gold stocks were unchanged Monday at 869,691 ounces, while COMEX silver stocks fell 21,296 ounces to 179,639,053 ounces.
COMEX September silver was seen opening 1.00 to 2.00 cents an ounce lower from Monday's close at $4.275.
On ACCESS September silver was last traded at $4.26 an ounce, off 1.50 cents from Monday's close, and vulnerable to further losses, dealers said.
NYMEX October platinum and NYMEX September palladium were both seen opening flat to down 50 cents an ounce, after closing at $388.50 and $152.45 an ounce respectively on Monday.

German catalytic converter maker Degussa AG said on Tuesday it was confident Russian platinum group metals sales to the Western world were being resumed and supply flows should return to normal in second half 1997.
Dealers said shipments of much delayed 1997 Russian PGMs began earlier this month.
U.S. retail sales for June, forecast to increase by 0.2 percent from May's 0.1 percent drop, were due at 0830 EDT.
